minutes.headline: Committee voted to send the primary school air conditioning letter and learned of a large FY23 Chapter 70 increase.
minutes.summary: The School Committee met remotely, went into executive session for union negotiation strategy, approved minutes, a line item transfer, the FY23 calendar, school choice seats and a donation. The business manager reported a large Chapter 70 increase and lower expected health insurance growth. The superintendent said a revised FY23 budget would return on the 16th without the librarian elimination. A long curriculum and assessment presentation followed.

budget_items.what_was_said: Transfer from unemployment, out-of-district private placement tuition and health insurance surpluses to cover advertising, iPads for special education staff and IT needs.
Splitting out the cafeteria and music room would lower the first-year request, and ARPA funds were raised as an alternative source.
The general supply COVID account is negative and high school custodial overtime is low; everything else is on target.
A narrative and budget report on ESSER initiatives will be posted publicly.
The district anticipates a Chapter 70 increase driven by more low-income students moving to a higher category.
Insurance expected nearer six percent than the budgeted eight percent, partly offset by school choice.
A state bill could fund masks, test kits and some local COVID costs.
Five ninth-grade seats for next year plus three carried-over open seats.
A Box Tops donation to the Turkey Hill gift account.

what_happened.line: The School Committee voted 5-0 to amend and send a letter on primary school air conditioning, mentioning a possible two-year split and ARPA funds.
The business manager said the district expects a large FY23 Chapter 70 increase, driven by more low-income students moving to a higher category.
The superintendent said a revised FY23 budget will return on the 16th without eliminating the librarian position.
Health insurance is expected to rise nearer six percent than the eight percent budgeted, partly offset by school choice.
The committee also approved a line item transfer, the 2022-2023 calendar, five ninth-grade school choice seats and a Box Tops donation, all 5-0.

why_it_matters: Primary school air conditioning would be paid from town funds or ARPA money, so the letter to the select board and town manager may shape what residents are asked to fund.
State aid and health insurance are two of the inputs that decide how much of the FY23 school budget falls on the tax bill, and both were reported as moving in the district's favor.
watch_next: The revised FY23 budget, due at the committee's meeting on the 16th, to see whether the librarian position stays.
The March 2 agenda, where the mask policy is scheduled to be taken up.
